mechanism_narrative: The observed sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks, moving from -79.6% to -74.4%, indicates a continued recovery in consumer activity, leading to further increases in retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days (t-3w to t-0w).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in WORKPLACES mobility, surpassing a 5-point weekly gain, signals a stronger return to office work, which will drive associated retail and recreation activities during lunch breaks and after hours, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES mobility increases by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 23.3% to 19.4%) and increasing PARKS mobility (from -43.7% to -29.6%) suggests a shift in public behavior towards spending more time outside the home and engaging in leisure activities, which will spill over into retail and recreation, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease while PARKS mobility continues to increase, but RETAIL_REC does not show an upward trend over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As the region continues its reopening phase, the sustained increase in TRANSIT station visits (from -74.3% to -66.9%) indicates greater public confidence and necessity for movement, directly correlating with increased foot traffic in retail and recreation areas over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility continues its upward trend in a reopening regime, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -39.1% to -32.0%), indicating increased essential outings, will naturally lead to more incidental retail and recreation stops, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility continues to increase, but RETAIL_REC does not show a corresponding increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PARKS mobility, exceeding a 7-point weekly gain (as observed from t-1w to t-0w), signifies a strong public desire for outdoor activity and movement, which will translate into increased visits to nearby retail and recreation establishments within the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 7 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility rises by more than 7 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent rise in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility over the last four weeks indicates a broader return to daily routines involving commuting and out-of-home work, which will inevitably boost retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks as people integrate leisure into their commutes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show week-on-week increases
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility increase week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, especially falling below 20% (as observed at t-0w), indicates people are spending less time at home, freeing up time for out-of-home activities including retail and recreation, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease below 20% in a reopening regime, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.
